verses.text: “I’m telling you the truth: anyone who sneaks into the sheep pen some other way instead of coming through the gate is a thief and a robber.
The one who comes in through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens for him. The sheep hear his voice; he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought his own sheep out, he walks ahead of them. They follow because they recognize his voice. 🐑
They won’t follow a stranger. They’ll run from him, because a stranger’s voice is unfamiliar to them.”
Jesus told them this story, but they didn’t get what he meant.
So Jesus explained again: “I’m telling you the truth: I am the gate for the sheep.
All those who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. Anyone who comes in through me will be saved. They’ll come and go and find good pasture.
A thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so they could have life—life overflowing. ✨
“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
A hired worker isn’t the shepherd and doesn’t own the sheep. When he sees a wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs. Then the wolf snatches them and scatters the flock.
He runs because he’s only there for the pay and doesn’t really care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and they know me—
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. I lay down my life for the sheep.
I have other sheep that don’t belong to this sheep pen. I have to bring them too. They’ll hear my voice, and there will be one flock with one shepherd.
The Father loves me because I lay down my life so I can take it up again.
No one takes it from me. I lay it down by my own choice. I have authority to lay it down, and authority to take it up again. This is the command I received from my Father.”
These words caused another split among the Jewish leaders.
Many of them said, “He has a demon and he’s out of his mind! Why are you listening to him?”
Others said, “Those aren’t the words of someone with a demon. Could a demon open the eyes of a blind person?”
The Festival of Dedication was happening in Jerusalem.
It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple area, in Solomon’s Colonnade.
The Jewish leaders gathered around him and said, “How long will you keep us guessing? If you’re the Messiah, say it plainly.”
Jesus answered, “I already told you, but you don’t believe me. The works I do in my Father’s name speak for me.
But you don’t believe because you aren’t among my sheep, as I told you.
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
I give them eternal life. They will never perish, and no one can snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all. No one can snatch them from the hand of my Father.
I and the Father are one.”
The Jewish leaders picked up stones again, ready to stone him.
Jesus said to them, “I’ve shown you many good works from my Father. Which one of those works are you stoning me for?”
They answered, “We’re not stoning you for a good work. We’re stoning you for blasphemy: you’re only a man, yet you make yourself God.”
Jesus replied, “Doesn’t your Law say, ‘I said, you are gods’?
If Scripture called those people ‘gods’—the ones who received God’s word—and Scripture can’t be undone,
why are you calling the one the Father set apart and sent into the world a blasphemer because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
If I’m not doing the works of my Father, don’t believe me.
But if I am doing them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works. Then you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father.”
They tried to seize him again, but he slipped away from them.
Jesus crossed the Jordan again and went to the place where John had first been baptizing. He stayed there.
Many people came to him. They said, “John didn’t perform any signs, but everything John said about this man was true.”
And many people there believed in him.
